title: Performance portability via C++ PSTL, SYCL, OpenMP, and HIP: the Gaia AVU-GSR case study
problem: The LSQR algorithm in the ESA Gaia AVU-GSR code must compute astrometric parameters for ~10^8 stars while running efficiently across diverse GPU architectures (NVIDIA and AMD) without significant performance degradation.
motivation: As applications targeting ExaFLOP-scale computing proliferate with each supercomputer being a unique project, computational languages portable across diverse GPU architectures without performance losses are increasingly necessary for HPC.
method: The authors rewrote the LSQR algorithm (which computes astrometric parameters—measurements of star positions—for ~10^8 stars) in five GPU programming frameworks: CUDA, C++ PSTL, SYCL, OpenMP, and HIP. They tested each version on five GPU platforms from NVIDIA and AMD, verifying that all versions produced correct results. Performance consistency across different hardware and problem sizes was measured using ȹ, the harmonic mean (an average that emphasizes consistent rather than peak performance) of performance efficiency.
key_novelty: This work systematically compares performance portability—how efficiently GPU code runs when switching between different hardware makers—across five programming frameworks (CUDA, C++ PSTL, SYCL, OpenMP, and HIP) tested on NVIDIA and AMD platforms.
contributions: Ported and tuned the LSQR algorithm using CUDA, C++ PSTL, SYCL, OpenMP, and HIP on five GPU platforms
Measured performance portability (ȹ): HIP 0.94, SYCL+AdaptiveCpp 0.93, CUDA 0.97 on NVIDIA, C++ PSTL 0.62
Demonstrated HIP as the most portable solution with strong cross-architecture performance
Validated portability findings' relevance beyond astrophysics to broad HPC applications

metrics.other: Performance portability ȹ (harmonic mean): HIP 0.94, SYCL+AdaptiveCpp 0.93, CUDA 0.97, C++ PSTL 0.62

primary_theme: GPU performance portability across programming models
